text:
alex: Support reported: Python quickstart failing for beginners. README snippet uses `prompt=` but the SDK expects `input=` so they get a TypeError. They copied straight into a script and hit: TypeError: create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'prompt'

harpreet: can you paste the snippet?

alex: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.responses.create(prompt="Hello world")
print(resp.output)
```

jen: oof. We changed the param name in v1.2 to `input` to align with the rest of the SDKs, but forgot to update the quickstart. Two options: add a tiny compatibility note + example using `input=` OR update snippet to `input=`. I'd prefer updating the snippet to be correct + add a note saying "If you're using an older SDK (<v1.2), rename `input` -> `prompt`."

harpreet: agree. Also add a one-liner to show env var export and minimal requirements: `pip install redwood-inference==1.*` so newbies don't have mismatched versions.

docsy-bot: Reminder: link PR to docs/quickstart label and include SDK minimum version. Also consider adding a unit test that validates quickstart snippets during CI to prevent future drift.

alex: i'll open PR #4302 updating the README snippet to use `input=` and adding the compatibility note + pip line.

jen: tiny nit: use `if __name__ == \"__main__\":` in sample so people run it as a script. Saves confusion when they paste into REPL.

harpreet: LGTM, merging once CI passes. Thanks for catching this, alex.

docsy-bot: Suggested follow-up: run a grep across other language quickstarts for parameter name mismatches and file issues to a backlog ticket.
